rows.34:1328:
Even if you try to change your fate, it won't change easily.
You have to struggle for it: hard work, study, self-control.
Even then, if such a thing as fate exists, I can't imagine it changing easily.
...But you know, there is an easy way.
At least, a way that leaves the person themselves satisfied.
Can you guess what it is?
It's relying on objects.
It's very common these days, isn't it?
Power stones, tachyon goods, pyramid power.
Things of that sort, said to hold supernatural powers.
By relying on such things, people try to change their fate and carve out a bright future.
What comes of leaning entirely on outside powers without making any effort...
Anyone with a brain should know that already.
{a}{f:|}, isn't there someone like that around you?
Someone who's become obsessed with that sort of mysterious power.
There's one in my class.
A pitiful person who has fallen under the spell of that kind of magic.{p}
rows.34:4ce8:
But she did become happy.
It was a world apart from Okazaki's case.
It couldn't be helped, after all.
In Okazaki's case, she didn't know Rubelize was a power stone that brings happiness, did she?
So she didn't know how to use it.
It just happened to grant her wish, that's all.
But Okawa's case was different.
Even if it was a devil's stone, she didn't use it the wrong way.
So there was no way she wouldn't be happy.{p}
